data_section_full_text:
The sample includes all firm-years between 1980 and 1992 with available data on
Value Line, Spectrum, COMPUSTAT, and the Center for Research in Security


CAR Vol. 18 No. 2 (Summer 2001)

222 Contemporary Accounting Research


Prices (CRSP). The final sample consists of 10,380 firm-years, with 673–973
observations per year.

Forecasts of future earnings, book values, and prices are obtained from the
University of Michigan Value Line data base, which contains electronic versions of
Value Line reports for the years 1978–92. Using the Value Line report issued during
the third quarter of a firm’s fiscal year, forecasts are available for the next fiscal year,
the year after, and a long-range forecast labeled “three-to-five years” ahead. Following AB, these three-to-five-year forecasts are assumed to be forecasts for four years
ahead. A three-year-ahead forecast is also required by the model, and is obtained by
interpolating between the two-year-ahead and four-year-ahead forecasts. The forecast
of long-run value is calculated by first multiplying the long-range P / E forecast by the
long-range earnings forecast to obtain a predicted price four years hence. Then, the
difference between this price and the long-range forecast of book value (which
yields the four-year-ahead terminal value) is added to expected abnormal earnings
two to four years ahead to obtain the long-term value component. The firm-specific
discount rate used to calculate the present value of future earnings and the terminal
value is calculated using the capital asset pricing model (CAPM) with firm-specific
betas and an assumed risk premium over the risk-free rate of 8 percent (AB). <sup>11</sup>

Historical book values and many of the control variables are obtained from the
1997 COMPUSTAT Annual Files. The price at the end of the firm’s second quarter,
cumulative size-adjusted abnormal returns, and data for some of the control variables are collected from the 1997 CRSP Daily Return Files. The price at the end of
the second quarter is used to roughly correspond with the date of the Value Line
forecast. Buy-and-hold size-adjusted returns are calculated as the difference
between the cumulative raw returns of the firm over a given horizon and the contemporaneous return on an equally weighted size decile control portfolio using all
available NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ firms. The returns are cumulated starting
at the end of the third quarter to ensure that all of the information in the Value Line
forecast has been impounded in price (AB). The institutional investor holdings
data are obtained from the Harvard Business School Spectrum data base, which
contains all SEC Form 13(f) filings between 1980 and 1997. The holdings data are
collected at the end of the third calendar quarter, which is the first holdings date
available after the release of the Value Line forecasts.

Institutions are classified based on investment horizon
